pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:17 The approve() source guard reads raw text without stripping comments. The body it slices already quotes the forbidden form in a comment (useDevTabNeedAnalysis.ts:101), and its absence leg matches only one spelling of the bare r.ok gate. The guard is open in the permissive direction for its presence probe, and a differently-spaced form slips past its absence probe. This is a construction-level gap: nothing currently evades it.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:17 The haystack is not normalised to executing code. Other repo guards use comment strippers, but this one does not. A comment naming runAction('approve', …) would satisfy the presence regex at line 27.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:29 This blocking absence check is evaded by `if(r.ok){`, by a braceless `if (r.ok)` or by a destructured `ok`. Unrecognised forms are not refused. The presence leg at line 27 carries most of the weight.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:20 The guard asserts its slice anchor exists before judging the body, so a renamed function fails loudly instead of slicing an empty string.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevTab.approve-error.test.ts:23 The rule that every DevTab write surfaces its failure is mechanised for approve() rather than left as prose.

pairs.evidence: app/api/tasks/tasks-route-tenancy.test.ts:71 The route-contract test proves each task route 'resolves a tenant via withWorkspace' with a bare-token regex over raw source. The import line (for example app/api/tasks/seen/route.ts:3) satisfies it on its own, so for seen/ and history/, whose other patterns only check that a `ws` argument is threaded, a handler that dropped the wrapper but kept the import and a local `ws` would pass.

techniques.evidence: app/api/tasks/tasks-route-tenancy.test.ts:71 Raw text with no normalisation. The needle appears in the import, so this leg cannot tell 'imported' from 'wraps the handler'.
app/api/tasks/tasks-route-tenancy.test.ts:90 The ordering assertion first proves both needles exist, so a reworded guard is a failure rather than a vacuous ordering pass.

app/api/profile/profile-spawn-timeout.test.ts:12 The 60s spawn bound is checked against the source shape rather than measured by waiting, which keeps a blocking unit gate deterministic given the tree.
